inShort: A feeds high balls and wide balls to B at the baseline. B drives the wide ones safely to the middle and goes for line or angle only with time.
rules: A and B stand at their baselines. A feeds every ball (hits or tosses it), B starts in the middle.
A mixes two kinds of ball, 8 per set: slower, higher balls B reaches in time, and wide balls B has to run for.
Higher ball with time: B may drive it down the line or short cross-court.
Wide ball: B drives it cross-court a little higher, toward the middle, just past the centre line. Then straight back to the middle.
Keep the full stroke, also when you take pace off: swing slower, don't stop short. On a wide ball, an open stance saves steps.
tooEasy: A gives no hint and mixes freely, and after a wide ball A feeds the next one into the opposite corner.
tooHard: A calls "wide" or "high" before each ball, so B can get ready.
goodLooksLike: Wide balls land just past the centre line, and B is back in the middle before A hits the next one.
